mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stop falling and begin a short-term recovery, weekday trips and pass-through footfall should lift RETAIL_REC within four weeks because commuting-linked visits create incidental shopping opportunities.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean after 4 weeks even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise versus t-0w for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed rise in RESIDENTIAL time displaces discretionary outings, so higher time at home should reduce RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks as households substitute away from shopping and entertainment trips.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean within 2 weeks after RESIDENTIAL rises for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS remain deeply below baseline, outdoor leisure is not substituting into retail-district visits; this should keep RETAIL_REC weak over the next four weeks because recreation demand stays suppressed rather than reallocating to shops and restaurants.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays below -25 points for 2 consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean despite PARKS remaining below -25 points for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals easing access and attendance norms; that interaction should raise RETAIL_REC over the next two to four weeks because both travel capacity and destination density increase together.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean within 4 weeks after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise week-on-week for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both strengthen while RETAIL_REC is still weak, this reflects a non-retail weekend and household activity mix that can spill into shopping trips one week later through routine errand consolidation.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -10 points while PARKS rises above -25 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher than its immediately prior weekly mean in the week after GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both clear the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently negative TRANSIT combined with flat WORKPLACES indicates weak commuting volume; that should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks because fewer workers are generating weekday retail demand.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean even though TRANSIT stays negative and WORKPLACES fails to improve for four consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A break in the downward trend of TRANSIT from one week to the next should precede a retail recovery within two weeks because access constraints are easing before consumers fully reprice their shopping routines.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases week-on-week after being below -18 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays at or below its prior 4-week mean for 2 weeks after TRANSIT posts a week-on-week increase from below -18 points.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, a simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL and drop in PARKS will compress discretionary mobility and lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks because people replace outside leisure with staying home.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean within 2 weeks while RESIDENTIAL rises and PARKS falls.
